profile: Plan an 18-day autumn trip to Japan for my wife and me, 10–27 November 2026. We land at Haneda at 19:45 and fly on to Shanghai at the end. We love ancient history, castles, the Edo period, nature, Ghibli and car culture, and we want two shopping days at the end. We're pescatarian, we'd like one ryokan night, we prefer fewer crowds, and we want to stay under 20k steps a day. Budget US$5,000–7,000.

# Japan, 10–27 November 2026 — Day-by-Day Itinerary (v4)

*Tokyo → Kawaguchiko (Mt Fuji, private hot-spring baths) → Kyoto → Tokyo → Shanghai. Updated 27 Oct 2026; day plans follow the PiQtour (Abby) method — purpose, anchors, one area, sit-downs, plan B.*

## Summary

- **18 days, 17 nights**, four places to sleep: Tokyo (same hotel twice), Fuji Lake Hotel (2 nights) and Konansou ryokan (1 night) at Kawaguchiko, and Kyoto next to Kyoto Station.
- **Estimated in-Japan cost for two: ≈ US$7,600** (¥1,246,400 at ¥164 = US$1), international flights, shopping and extra tickets excluded.
- **New in v4:** Tokyo 10–14 Nov → Kawaguchiko 14–17 Nov → Kyoto 17–23 Nov → Tokyo 23–27 Nov. Hakone, Tsumago, Kurama–Kibune and Ghibli Park are out; in come a Ueno museum day (Day 4) and three Fuji nights in rooms whose private open-air bath uses real hot-spring water with Fuji in view — two at Fuji Lake Hotel, then a ryokan night with kaiseki at Konansou. Kyoto goes from 8 to 6 nights; Days 10–18 are unchanged.
- **Over budget:** the estimate is now about US$7,600, above your US$7,000 ceiling. The three Fuji nights (≈¥270,000) cost about ¥230,000 more than the Tsumago night they replace, partly offset by two fewer Kyoto nights. To get back under US$7,000: value hotels in Tokyo (≈¥18,000 instead of ¥26,000 saves ≈¥64,000) and Kyoto, and breakfast-only at Fuji Lake Hotel one night.

### How each day is built (the PiQtour rules applied)

| Rule | How it shows up here |
|---|---|
| Start with *why* | Every day opens with a one-line purpose |
| Anchor the day on lunch and fixed-time bookings | “Anchors” per day: lunch spot, ticket slots, last entries |
| Respect business hours | Times checked against official hours where available (temples and gardens often close 16:00–17:00 in November) |
| One area a day, two connected at most | Day 15 and Day 17 trimmed; extras moved to “optional” |
| Leave buffer; force sit-downs | Every day has at least one “Sit” row (café, garden veranda, hotel break) |
| Ride instead of any walk over ~15 min | Taxi budget added; long hops are taxis or trains |
| Plan B, not orders from your past self | “If it rains or you’re tired” per day |
| Spend on location, fewer moves, taxis, guides; save on rooms | Hotels next to big stations; ryokan, Daikoku tour and SHIBUYA SKY are the deliberate splurges |

## Good to know

- **JR Pass:** Don’t buy one. The 7-day pass is ¥50,000 (¥53,000 via overseas agencies from 1 Oct 2026), and your Fuji legs (Fuji Excursion, Mishima bus) are partly or wholly outside it; single tickets cost less. (source)
- **Bags:** Two medium suitcases (size 140 or under) + two daypacks + a folding duffel for shopping. On 13 Nov send both suitcases from the Tokyo hotel to the Kyoto hotel and go to Kawaguchiko with daypacks; send them back to Tokyo the evening before you leave Kyoto. (source)
- **Luggage forwarding cost:** Tokyo ↔ Kyoto about ¥2,600–3,200 per bag depending on size and source; budget about ¥3,000. Delivery next day. (source)
- **Pescatarian eating:** Fish dashi is everywhere and fine for you. Watch for pork ramen broth (tonkotsu), gyoza, katsu, chicken in oden, and pork in okonomiyaki — ask for “buta nuki”. (source)
- **Ryokan note (write it):** 肉（牛・豚・鶏・馬）は食べられません。魚介類は大丈夫です。 — “We don’t eat meat (beef, pork, chicken, horse); fish and seafood are fine.” Avoid “vegetarian”: it’s ambiguous. (source)
- **Tax-free shopping:** From 1 Nov 2026 you pay full price and get the 10% back after showing the goods at airport customs before check-in. ¥5,000 minimum per shop. (source)
- **Money and transit:** Suica/PASMO on your phone for metros, buses and konbini. Carry ¥20,000–30,000 cash each for small temples, small shops and the Kawaguchiko loop buses. 7-Eleven ATMs take foreign cards.
- **Onsen:** Wash fully first, no swimsuits, towel out of the water. Many baths refuse visible tattoos; private family baths (kashikiri) solve this.
- **Etiquette:** Quiet on trains, no eating while walking in temple streets, carry your rubbish, don’t photograph geiko in Gion, stay on marked paths. (source)
- **New fees:** Kyoto hotel tax is tiered per person per night; Himeji Castle ¥2,500; departure tax ¥3,000 per person (in airline tickets booked from 1 Jul 2026). (source)
- **Weather:** Mid-to-late November is usually dry and clear, roughly 10–18 °C. Pack layers, a light down jacket for dawn starts, and waterproof shoes.

### Why Kawaguchiko now
Version 4 is built around **hot-spring baths with a view of Fuji**. At Kawaguchiko you get Fuji from your own bath, not just from a ropeway on a clear day, and many "private bath" rooms elsewhere use plain water. Both hotels are about 10 minutes from {{kawaguchiko-station}} and a few minutes from each other, so moving to the ryokan is easy.

**The timing works too.** The {{momiji}} is forecast to peak around **16 Nov**, your Day 7, and Tokyo's ginkgo peak around **26 Nov** falls in your last Tokyo days. Kyoto's centre peaks after you leave, so the Kyoto days favour higher ground at Takao.

**Left out, and what replaces it:**
- {{hakone}}: replaced by Kawaguchiko; {{tenjo-ropeway}} and the lake cruise give the views, {{sengen}} the history.
- {{tsumago}} and the Kiso Valley: their ryokan baths aren't hot springs. {{nenba}} gives you a thatched village instead.
- Chureito Pagoda: among the most crowded spots around Fuji. Do the {{momiji}} at dawn instead.
- {{ghibli-park}}, {{kurama}} and {{kibune}}: Kyoto lost two days. You still have the {{ghibli-museum}} on Day 16.

### Good to know
- **Pescatarian:** dashi (fish stock) is fine for you, so just avoid meat. Watch for tonkotsu (pork) ramen broth, gyoza, katsu, chicken in oden, and pork in okonomiyaki (ask for *buta nuki*, no pork). Kaiseki often includes beef or pork, so for both Kawaguchiko hotels write *"no meat (beef, pork, chicken, horse); fish and seafood are fine"* rather than "vegetarian".
- **Tax-free shopping (new from 1 Nov 2026):** you pay full price and get the refund at departure. Take your purchases to the customs tax-free terminal **before check-in**. The minimum is ¥5,000 per shop.
- **Money:** carry ¥20–30k each in cash for small temples, small shops and the Kawaguchiko loop buses. 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards.
- **Onsen:** wash fully before getting in, no swimsuits, keep your towel out of the water. Your private baths at Fuji avoid tattoo rules altogether.
- **Fuji foothills:** bears have been sighted, so stay on marked paths and finish forest walks well before dusk (sunset is about 16:30).
- **Weather:** usually dry and clear, about 10–18 °C, colder at Kawaguchiko in the mornings. Bring a light down jacket.
